forces: R14 specifies the path-class-widening scenario but no rule implements it: no widen or benign logic, no diagnostic id, and no acknowledgement field exist in the checker or the signed-record shape, so an unacknowledged weakening is caught only by a human noticing (#203).
Widening is the cheap direction: moving a path into documentation_only lowers what governance demands of every future change touching it, which is precisely the weakening R14 exists to catch.

The assessment schema is closed, so the acknowledgement cannot ride there without a schema version bump; the signed governance record is the natural carrier, and its records tolerate additive optional fields.

A candidate checker is never the sole judge of whether it weakened itself: the rule must live in the checker code the trusted baseline runs, so the dual check's baseline-candidate asymmetry judges both the policy and any future edit to the rule.

The checker already has the needed machinery: a --base option, blobAt for reading files at any ref, trackedPaths for the tracked universe, classifyPath for classification, and the checkSchemaEvolution precedent for comparing a candidate artifact against its merge-base copy.

forces: The assessment schema is closed, so the acknowledgement cannot ride there without a schema version bump; the signed governance record is the natural carrier, and its records tolerate additive optional fields.
approach-acknowledgement-in-assessment.reason: The assessment is authored before implementation and before review; the acknowledgement is a reviewer act that must bind an exact reviewed commit, which is what the signed record exists to do. Recording it in the assessment would also demand a closed-schema version bump for an artifact that is the wrong carrier.

forces: Widening is the cheap direction: moving a path into documentation_only lowers what governance demands of every future change touching it, which is precisely the weakening R14 exists to catch.
approach-changed-paths-only-detection.reason: A pattern edit can reclassify paths the commit range never touches, so restricting detection to changed paths would miss exactly the silent, broad reclassification the scenario exists to reject; the tracked universe is the only complete basis.

evidence_ids: path events are computed by classifying the tracked universe under both policies, keyed by path, firing only when the candidate class is documentation_only and the baseline class was not
pattern events are keyed pattern:<pattern> for documentation_only patterns absent from the baseline policy
self-governance fixtures assert path-class-widening-unacknowledged for both event kinds
exactly one signed record may carry pathClassWideningAcknowledgement, with acknowledged true, the actual comparison baselineCommit, a substantive reason, and an exact path-key set
fixtures assert the absent, ambiguous, invalid, stale, and incomplete diagnostics separately
strengthening moves, narrowing moves, and policy edits that change no classification produce no widening event
fixtures assert a narrowing and an unrelated policy edit pass without the diagnostic

security_justification.trust_boundary: The rule reads only repository Git objects and tracked paths; it introduces no new trust boundary, credential, or external input surface.
security_justification.authority_provenance: Does not modify authority or signing logic; the acknowledgement is data read from the existing signed-record source, whose binding to an exact commit the review-freshness verifier already enforces.
security_justification.authentication_or_authorization: Does not modify or interact with authentication or authorization mechanisms; the checker remains actor-neutral and dependency-free.
security_justification.audit_integrity: Strengthens audit integrity: every rejection carries a distinct named diagnostic, and every acceptance path is bound to an exact baseline and an exact event set, leaving a reviewable trail.
security_justification.confidentiality: Processes no secrets, personal data, or restricted material; diagnostics name repository paths and class names only.
security_justification.mutation_ownership: Changes are confined to the declared owned paths: the new checker module, its call site, the dual-check driver, the self-governance test file, the actor-neutral document, and the change directory.
security_justification.fail_posture: Fails closed: an unreadable baseline policy or record source yields a rejection, never a pass; the acknowledgement must match exactly rather than merely exist.
security_justification.error_disclosure: Diagnostics are bounded strings naming paths, classes, and patterns; no stack traces, tokens, or environment data are emitted.
security_justification.concurrency: The checker is a single-threaded read-only process; the new module adds no concurrency, no shared state, and no non-deterministic ordering (code-point sorts throughout).
security_justification.lifecycle: Runs in the existing implementation and final checker phases and the dual check; no new lifecycle stage or CI job is introduced.
security_justification.resource_retention: One extra tracked-path enumeration and one baseline blob read per run; both are bounded and released with the process.
security_justification.retry_or_redelivery: No retry or redelivery behavior is introduced; the rule is deterministic on identical inputs.
security_justification.cryptography: Does not introduce, modify, or rely upon cryptographic algorithms or keys; baseline commits are compared as opaque object ids.
security_justification.privacy_transformation: Processes no user telemetry, personal data, or operational payloads; only repository-internal path and policy data is inspected.
security_justification.external_security_integration: No external security integration, network access, or new tool invocation is introduced.
